text: The original attention mechanism divides the query‑key dot products by a constant (specifically \(1/\sqrt{d_k}\)) before applying softmax to prevent the dot products from becoming too large when the dimensionality \(d_k\) is large. Large dot products push the softmax into regions with very small gradients, which hampers learning. Scaling the dot products keeps them in a range where the softmax has useful gradients and improves training stability. [C:attention:10]

The smoothing module turns the discrete chunk‑boundary decisions into a differentiable operation, thereby restoring gradient flow that would otherwise be blocked by the hard chunking decisions. This stabilises training dynamics and prevents large fluctuations in compression ratios during optimisation. [C:dynchunk:22] [C:dynchunk:8]
The paper describes a three‑stage hierarchy: a 0‑stage isotropic model, a 1‑stage model, and a 2‑stage model that recursively nests the chunking strategy. [C:dynchunk:78]

Moshi’s Inner Monologue is a training and inference procedure that jointly models text and audio tokens. It first predicts time‑aligned text tokens as a prefix to the audio tokens, allowing the model to exploit the knowledge from the text modality while remaining a speech‑to‑speech system. This hierarchical semantic‑to‑acoustic token generation improves linguistic quality and enables streaming speech recognition and text‑to‑speech by simply adjusting the delay between text and audio tokens.
